newsitem.title: ITALY: Reuters Asset Allocation Poll (Italy) - March 27.
newsitem.headline: Reuters Asset Allocation Poll (Italy) - March 27.

text.p: Italian banks and investment funds have improved their outlook on Italian financial markets, especially bonds after the sharp drop in futures Btp over the past month, but they reduced their investments abroad, an Italian Reuter Asset Allocation Poll for April showed.
"In the past few weeks Italy has been under a lot of pressure, maybe too much. It is difficult for this condition to continue with the current momentum," Alessando Fugnoli, strategist at Caboto said.

"Sooner or later things will calm down. The fall in inflation and the fact Italy will arithmetically reach 3.0 percent (deficit/GDP ratio required by the Maastricht Treaty for EMU) will give Italian markets scope for improvement ," he added.

"Over the last two months we reduced our portfolio weight on Italian bonds because we feared a sharp drop, now we think the market has what it takes to start rising again," Alfredo Granata, analyst at Banca di Roma said adding that the "current price levels are interesting to come back into the market."
The Btp future on February 25 touched a high of 130.75 and at 1415 GMT on Thursday it was down six basis points at 125.30.
The risk analysis department at Cariplo, on the other hand, maintained the same weight on Italian bonds but increased its exposure on the Italian stock exchange.

"If European monetary union proceeds, Italian market rates can only decrease. This will help the economy and an official interest rate cut and will improve the outlook for Italian companies," Cariplo said.
Banco di Sardegna SARI.MI reduced by five percent its exposure to Italian equities in favour of foreign markets (15 percent in bonds and 10 percent in equities).

"We are still positive on Italian equities but we think the equilibrium level for the Mibtel index is around 12,000-12,200," Barbara Giani, analyst at the Sardinian bank said. "It would be favourable to invest in the stock market at slightly lower levels, but otherwise we'd rather take profit," she added.
At 1445 GMT, the Mibtel was up 126 points at 12,097.

Banca Commerciale Italiana increased its weight in cash and reduced its exposure on Italian stocks and bonds. "Cash yields more and is less risky," Marcello Esposito, analyst at BCI said. "For cash we don't mean short term bonds (BOTs) but rather, repos and Libor," he added.

The survey showed banks and funds reduced their exposure to core European and U.S. markets. "We don't think the U.S. or German market will perform well over the next months and the relative weakening of the lira makes foreign markets less attractive," Granata of Banca di Roma said. "We prefer non-core European markets because the convergence process will soon start again," he added.
Reuters collected allocation of a typical portfolio in lire from 10 Italian banks and investment funds from March 24-26.
